operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of timelog entries.

This operation provides employees with access to their own timelogs, while users with time:view_all permission can view all employees' timelogs across the organization. Supports comprehensive filtering by date range, project, task, billable status, and employee.

Timelogs included in approved timesheets are locked and cannot be modified, but remain visible in the list. Results are paginated with configurable page sizes and sorting options by date, duration, or creation timestamp.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_platform_timelogs table with pagination and filtering.

Apply organization context filter: join with hrm_platform_employees to scope results to current organization.

Apply permission-based employee filter: if user lacks time:view_all, filter by employee_id = current user's employee id.

Apply optional filters from request body: date range (date >= fromDate AND date <= toDate), project_id, task_id, billable boolean, employee_id (for managers).

Join with hrm_platform_projects for project name, hrm_platform_tasks for task title, hrm_platform_employees for employee name.

Include timesheet status indicator: join with hrm_platform_timesheets to determine if timelog is in approved status (locked).

Support cursor-based pagination with take/skip parameters. Sort by date DESC by default, allow sorting by duration_minutes, created_at.

Return IHrmPlatformTimelog.ISummary for each item with embedded project and task summaries.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of timelog summaries with project and task information

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for timelog filtering

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific time entry record by its unique identifier.

This operation returns the complete timelog entity including the employee who logged the time, the project and optional task the work was performed against, the work date, duration in minutes, optional description, and billable status. Also includes metadata such as creation and update timestamps.

Timelogs are the fundamental unit of time measurement in the system, capturing granular work session data. This endpoint provides access to individual time entry details for viewing, auditing, or integration purposes.

Access control: Employees can view their own timelogs. Users with the time:view_all permission can view any employee's timelogs within the organization. Timelogs included in approved timesheets are locked and immutable.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query hrm_platform_timelogs table by UUID primary key. Return the complete timelog record including all fields: id, employee_id, project_id, task_id, timesheet_id, date, duration_minutes, description, billable, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. Verify the timelog exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null). Join with hrm_platform_employees, hrm_platform_projects, and hrm_platform_tasks if needed for authorization checks. Ensure the requesting user has permission to view this timelog (either owns it or has time:view_all permission). Return 404 if timelog not found or access denied.

responseBody.description: Complete timelog entity with all fields

parameters.description: UUID identifier of the timelog to retrieve
parameters.name: timelogId

operations.description:
Create a new time entry record (timelog) for the authenticated employee.

This operation allows employees to log work time against a specific project with an optional task assignment. Each timelog captures the date work was performed, duration in minutes, optional description of work done, and whether the time is billable to a client.

Employees can only create timelogs for themselves and only for projects they are assigned to as project members. If a task is specified, it must belong to the selected project. The billable flag defaults to true if not provided.

Timelogs cannot be created for dates that fall within a week where the employee already has a submitted or approved timesheet, as those periods are locked for modifications. New timelogs are created without timesheet assignment and can be included in a draft timesheet later.

This operation supports soft delete - deleted timelogs are marked with a deleted_at timestamp rather than being permanently removed from the database. Deleted timelogs are excluded from normal queries unless explicitly requested.

Upon successful creation, the system broadcasts a real-time event to users with time:view_all permission for live list updates.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new timelog entry for the authenticated employee.

1. Extract employee ID from authenticated session context
2. Validate request body:
   - date: required, valid date format
   - durationMinutes: required, positive integer (> 0)
   - projectId: required, valid UUID
   - taskId: optional, valid UUID if provided
   - description: optional, string if provided
   - billable: optional, boolean, defaults to true
3. Verify employee is assigned to the specified project (check hrm_platform_project_members)
4. If taskId provided, verify task belongs to the specified project
5. Check if date falls within a submitted or approved timesheet week for this employee - if so, reject (timelog would be locked)
6. Insert new record into hrm_platform_timelogs:
   - id: generate UUID
   - employee_id: from session
   - project_id: from request
   - task_id: from request or null
   - timesheet_id: null (not yet in timesheet)
   - date: from request
   - duration_minutes: from request
   - description: from request or null
   - billable: from request or true
   - created_at: current timestamp
   - updated_at: current timestamp
   - deleted_at: null
7. Generate timelog.created real-time event with payload including date, duration, project, task, description, billable
8. Return created timelog entity

responseBody.description: The newly created timelog entity with all fields including generated ID and timestamps

requestBody.description: Timelog creation data including work date, duration, project assignment, and optional task and description

prerequisites.description: Project must exist before time can be logged against it. The projectId in the timelog request must reference a valid project.
Employee must be assigned to the project as a project member before logging time. The operation validates project membership via hrm_platform_project_members table.
If taskId is provided in the timelog request, the task must exist and belong to the specified project. This prerequisite ensures the optional task reference is valid.

operations.description:
Update an existing timelog entry with modified work details.

This operation allows employees to edit their own timelogs or users with time:manage permission to edit any timelog in the organization. The timelog can be updated only if it is not part of an approved timesheet - timelogs in approved timesheets are locked and immutable.

When updating, the project must be one the employee is assigned to. If a task is specified, it must belong to the selected project. The billable flag indicates whether the time is chargeable to a client. Changes to the timelog update the updated_at timestamp and trigger a timelog updated event for real-time synchronization.

Attempting to modify a timelog in an approved timesheet results in a validation error. Similarly, assigning a project the employee is not a member of, or a task that doesn't belong to the project, will be rejected.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Retrieve the timelog by timelogId from hrm_platform_timelogs table.
2. Verify the timelog exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null).
3. Check timesheet lock status: if timesheet_id is not null, join with hrm_platform_timesheets and verify status is not 'approved'. If approved, reject with 422 error.
4. Authorization check: verify requester is either the employee who owns the timelog (employee_id matches) OR has time:manage permission in the organization.
5. Validate request body:
   - project_id: verify employee is assigned to this project (exists in hrm_platform_project_members)
   - task_id: if provided, verify it belongs to the project (task.project_id === request.project_id)
   - date: must be a valid date
   - duration_minutes: must be positive integer
   - billable: boolean value
6. Update the timelog record with provided fields, set updated_at to current timestamp.
7. Return the updated timelog entity with all fields.
8. Emit timelog updated event for real-time subscribers.

responseBody.description: The updated timelog entity with all fields including employee, project, task, and timesheet references.

parameters.description: UUID identifier of the timelog to update (global scope).
parameters.name: timelogId

requestBody.description: Update payload containing modifiable timelog fields. All fields are optional - only provided fields will be updated.

operations.description:
Permanently delete a timelog entry by removing it from the system.

This operation allows employees to delete their own timelog entries, or users with time:manage permission to delete any employee's timelogs. Deletion is subject to timesheet status restrictions: employees cannot delete timelogs that are part of submitted or approved timesheets, while users with time:manage permission can delete any timelog regardless of timesheet status.

The timelog is soft-deleted by setting the deleted_at timestamp. Upon successful deletion, a timelog deletion event is generated to update real-time views. The deleted timelog is removed from all active timelog lists and timesheet calculations.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Delete a timelog by ID with authorization and timesheet status validation.

1. Retrieve timelog from hrm_platform_timelogs table by timelogId
2. Verify requester authorization:
   - If requester is the timelog's employee: check timesheet status
   - If requester has time:manage permission: allow regardless of timesheet status
3. For non-managers, query hrm_platform_timesheets to check timesheet status:
   - If timesheet_id is NULL or timesheet status is 'draft': allow deletion
   - If timesheet status is 'submitted' or 'approved': reject with 403 error
4. Perform soft delete by setting deleted_at to current timestamp
5. Generate timelog deletion event for real-time list updates
6. Return 204 No Content on success

Edge cases:
- Timelog not found: return 404
- Timelog already deleted: return 404
- Unauthorized (not owner and no time:manage permission): return 403
- In submitted/approved timesheet without time:manage: return 403

parameters.description: UUID identifier of the timelog to delete
parameters.name: timelogId

prerequisites.description: Timelog must be created before it can be deleted

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of timesheet records within the authenticated user's organization context.

This operation provides advanced search capabilities for timesheets including status filtering (draft, submitted, approved, rejected), week date range filtering, and employee-specific queries. Permission-based access control applies: employees can view their own timesheets by default; users with time:view_all permission can view all timesheets across the organization; users with time:approve permission can view all submitted timesheets for approval workflow.

Supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options. Response includes timesheet summary information optimized for list displays, showing week period, status, total hours, and workflow timestamps. Only active (non-deleted) timesheets are included in results. Results are scoped to the authenticated user's organization through employee membership relationships.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query hrm_platform_timesheets table with pagination and filtering. Filter by status (draft, submitted, approved, rejected), week_start_date range, and employee_id (derived from authenticated session). Join with hrm_platform_employees for employee display name. Join with hrm_platform_timelogs to calculate total hours if not pre-computed. Apply organization isolation by filtering timesheets belonging to employees in the current organization context. Support cursor-based pagination for large result sets. Sort by week_start_date descending by default (most recent first). Return timesheet summary information optimized for list displays including status, week period, total hours, and submission/review timestamps.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of timesheet summaries with week period, status, total hours, and workflow metadata

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering timesheets by status, date range, and employee

operations.description:
Retrieve a single timesheet record by its unique identifier.

This operation returns the complete timesheet entity including week period (Monday to Sunday), workflow status (draft, submitted, approved, rejected), submission and review timestamps, and rejection reason if applicable. The response includes the owning employee details and the reviewer employee details when the timesheet has been reviewed.

Timesheets group an employee's timelogs by week for approval tracking. The included timelogs array contains all time entries associated with this timesheet. Approved timesheets have locked timelogs that cannot be edited or deleted.

Access is restricted to the timesheet owner (employee) or users with time:approve permission. Returns 404 if the timesheet does not exist or the user lacks permission to view it.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query hrm_platform_timesheets table by primary key id (UUID).

Join with hrm_platform_employees for employee relation to include employee details.
Left join with hrm_platform_employees for reviewedByEmployee relation to include reviewer details when present.

Include related timelogs from hrm_platform_timelogs table where timesheet_id matches.

Validate that the requesting user has permission to view this timesheet:
- Employee can view their own timesheets
- Users with time:approve permission can view all timesheets

Return 404 if timesheet not found or user lacks permission.
Return 400 if timesheet is soft-deleted (deleted_at is not null).

responseBody.description: Complete timesheet entity with employee, reviewer, and timelogs

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the timesheet (UUID format)
parameters.name: timesheetId

operations.description:
Create a new draft timesheet for the authenticated employee's weekly time tracking.

This operation creates a timesheet in draft status for a specific week period. The employee must provide both the week start date (Monday) and week end date (Sunday) in ISO date format. Upon creation, all existing timelogs for the employee within the specified week are automatically associated with the timesheet.

Only one timesheet per employee per week is allowed due to the unique constraint on employee_id and week_start_date. Attempting to create a duplicate timesheet for an existing week will result in a constraint violation error. Draft timesheets remain editable until submitted for approval.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Create a new draft timesheet for the authenticated employee. Extract employee_id from session context. Validate no existing timesheet for the same employee and week_start_date (check unique constraint). Calculate week_end_date as week_start_date + 6 days (Monday to Sunday). Set initial status to 'draft'. Set submitted_at, reviewed_at, reviewed_by_employee_id, rejection_reason to null. Automatically associate all existing timelogs for this employee within the week date range by updating their timesheet_id. Return the created timesheet with full entity data. Handle constraint violation error if timesheet for this week already exists.

responseBody.description: Created timesheet entity in draft status

requestBody.description: Timesheet creation data with week period dates

operations.description:
Update an existing timesheet's metadata and configuration.

This operation allows employees to modify their draft or rejected timesheets. Updates are restricted to timesheets in 'draft' or 'rejected' status - submitted and approved timesheets cannot be modified to maintain approval workflow integrity.

Updatable fields include the week period (week_start_date and week_end_date) and rejection_reason. When updating week dates, the system validates that week_start_date falls on a Monday and week_end_date on the corresponding Sunday. The unique constraint ensures no duplicate timesheets exist for the same employee and week period.

For rejected timesheets, clearing the rejection_reason prepares the timesheet for resubmission. The operation returns the complete updated timesheet entity including employee and reviewer information.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Update a timesheet by UUID. Query hrm_platform_timesheets table by id. Validate timesheet exists and is not deleted. Check status is 'draft' or 'rejected' - reject updates to submitted/approved timesheets. Validate week_start_date is Monday and week_end_date is Sunday of same week. Validate unique constraint: no other timesheet exists for same employee_id and week_start_date combination. If status is 'rejected' and rejection_reason is being cleared, allow for resubmission. Update allowed fields: week_start_date, week_end_date, rejection_reason. Update updated_at timestamp. Return full timesheet entity. Join with employee and reviewedByEmployee for complete response.

responseBody.description: Updated timesheet entity with employee and reviewer details

requestBody.description: Timesheet update data with week period and rejection reason

prerequisites.description: Timesheet must be created before it can be updated. The POST operation creates a draft timesheet for the authenticated employee's weekly time tracking.

operations.description:
Soft delete a draft timesheet from the system.

This operation allows employees to delete their own draft timesheets before submission. Only timesheets with 'draft' status can be deleted - submitted, approved, or rejected timesheets are locked and cannot be removed. Users with time:manage permission can delete any employee's draft timesheets.

The deletion is implemented as a soft delete, marking the timesheet with a deletion timestamp while preserving data integrity. All timelogs associated with the deleted timesheet are also soft deleted through cascade. The operation validates ownership and status before proceeding, returning appropriate error responses for invalid deletion attempts.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification: Soft delete a timesheet by setting deleted_at timestamp. Validate that timesheet status is 'draft' - reject deletion attempts on submitted, approved, or rejected timesheets with 400 Bad Request. Verify the requesting employee owns this timesheet (employee_id matches authenticated user's employee ID) unless they have time:manage permission. Check that no timelogs in this timesheet are referenced elsewhere. Set deleted_at to current timestamp. Cascade soft delete to all associated timelogs in this timesheet week. Return the deleted timesheet entity. Log activity entry for timesheet deletion.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the timesheet to delete (UUID format)
parameters.name: timesheetId

prerequisites.description: Timesheet must be created before it can be deleted - the delete operation requires an existing timesheet entity with draft status

operations.description:
Update the currently running timer for the authenticated employee.

This operation allows employees to modify their active timer's description, project, or task selection while the timer continues running. Employees can change the project to any project they are assigned to, and can add, change, or remove the task selection. If a task is specified, it must belong to the selected project.

The timer continues running without interruption during updates. All modifications take effect immediately and are reflected in real-time through running timer updates events. This endpoint is commonly used when employees need to adjust their time tracking context during a work session.
operations.name: patch
operations.specification: Query hrm_platform_timers table filtering by authenticated employee's ID. Validate that a running timer exists for the employee. Validate project_id references a project the employee is assigned to (check hrm_platform_project_members). If task_id is provided, validate it belongs to the specified project. Update the timer record with new description, project_id, and/or task_id values. Emit running timer updates event with modified fields. Return updated timer entity. Handle edge cases: no active timer (404), invalid project assignment (400), task-project mismatch (400).

responseBody.description: The updated timer entity with new field values.

requestBody.description: Update criteria for the running timer. All fields are optional; only provided fields will be updated.

prerequisites.description: Project must exist before a timer can reference it for time tracking
Employee must be assigned to the project before tracking time on it per business validation rules
Task must exist before a timer can optionally reference it for granular time tracking
Timer must be created and running before it can be updated with new configuration

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific timer by its unique identifier.

This operation returns the complete timer entity including the start timestamp, associated project, optional task, work description, and ownership information. Timers represent real-time tracking sessions that employees use to capture work duration as it happens.

The timer includes references to the employee who owns it, the project being tracked, and optionally the specific task. Elapsed duration is calculated from the started_at timestamp to the current time, not stored as a separate field. When stopped, timers convert to timelog entries with calculated duration.

Access is restricted to the timer owner or users with appropriate permissions within the organization context. Only one active timer can exist per employee at any time.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query hrm_platform_timers table by UUID id parameter.

Retrieve full timer entity including: id, employee_id, project_id, task_id (nullable), started_at, description (nullable), created_at, updated_at, deleted_at.

Join with hrm_platform_projects to include project details in response.
Join with hrm_platform_tasks if task_id is present to include task details.

Validate timer exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null).
Enforce organization context - timer must belong to the authenticated user's current organization.
Enforce access control - only timer owner or users with time:manage permission can access.

Return 404 if timer not found or access denied.
Return 400 if timerId is not valid UUID format.

responseBody.description: Complete timer entity with project and optional task references

operations.description:
Start a new real-time timer for time tracking.

This operation creates an active timer session for the authenticated employee. The timer records the start timestamp, selected project, optional task, and optional work description. Each employee can have at most one active timer at a time - attempting to start a new timer while one is already running will be rejected.

The project must be one the employee is assigned to as a project member. If a task is specified, it must belong to the selected project. The timer continues running indefinitely until the employee explicitly stops or discards it.

When the timer is later stopped, a timelog entry is automatically created with the calculated duration rounded to the nearest minute.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new timer record for the authenticated employee.

1. Extract employee_id from authentication context (session token)
2. Check if employee already has an active timer (query hrm_platform_timers where employee_id equals current employee and deleted_at is null)
3. If active timer exists, reject with 409 Conflict error
4. Validate project_id: verify employee is a member of the project (query hrm_platform_project_members where employee_id and project_id match)
5. If task_id is provided, validate it belongs to the specified project (query hrm_platform_tasks where id equals task_id and project_id equals project_id)
6. Create timer record with: id (UUID), employee_id, project_id, task_id (nullable), started_at (current timestamp), description (nullable), created_at, updated_at
7. Return the created timer entity

Edge cases:
- Employee not assigned to project → 400 Bad Request
- Task does not belong to project → 400 Bad Request
- Active timer already exists → 409 Conflict
- Project does not exist → 404 Not Found
- Task does not exist → 404 Not Found

responseBody.description: The created timer entity with all fields

requestBody.description: Timer creation parameters including required project and optional task and description

prerequisites.description: Project must be created before a timer can track time against it. The project_id in timer creation request must reference an existing project.

Employee must be assigned as a project member before starting a timer. The timer creation validates that the employee is a member of the specified project, rejecting with 400 Bad Request if not assigned.

operations.description:
Update the configuration of a running timer.

This operation allows employees to modify their active timer's project, task, or description while the timer is running. Employees can switch to a different project they are assigned to, change or remove the task selection, or update the work description.

The timer must be owned by the requesting employee. Project changes require the employee to be assigned to the new project. Task changes require the task to belong to the currently selected project. The task can be removed entirely or added to a timer that previously had no task.

Validation ensures the timer exists, is not deleted, and belongs to the authenticated employee. Project and task assignments are verified against the employee's project memberships.
operations.name: putByTimerid
operations.specification: Query hrm_platform_timers table by timerId UUID parameter. Verify timer exists, deleted_at is null, and employee_id matches authenticated user's employee record. For project_id updates: verify employee has project membership in the new project via hrm_platform_project_members. For task_id updates: verify task belongs to the selected project and employee has project membership. Update description, project_id, task_id fields as provided. Set updated_at to current timestamp. Return complete IHrmPlatformTimer entity with all fields including started_at, description, project_id, task_id. Handle edge cases: timer not found (404), timer already deleted (404), employee not owner (403), project assignment invalid (400), task-project mismatch (400).

responseBody.description: Updated timer entity with modified configuration

requestBody.description: Timer configuration fields to update

prerequisites.description: Project must exist before being referenced by a timer's project_id field
Task must exist within the project before being referenced by a timer's task_id field
Timer must be created before it can be updated

operations.description:
Discard a running timer without creating a timelog entry.

This operation soft deletes an employee's active timer by setting the deleted_at timestamp, without recording any time. Unlike stopping a timer, discarding does not create a timelog entry and the action effectively abandons the current tracking session without logging the elapsed time. This is useful when an employee started a timer by mistake or wants to abandon the current tracking session.

Only the timer owner (the employee who started the timer) can discard their own timer. The operation requires the timer to be in running state (deleted_at is null). Once discarded, the timer is marked as deleted and excluded from active timer queries. The soft delete allows for potential audit trail maintenance while removing the timer from active operations.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Delete the timer record from hrm_platform_timers table by timerId.

Validate that the timer exists and is owned by the requesting employee (employee_id matches authenticated user's employee record).

Verify the timer has not already been discarded (deleted_at is null).

Perform cascade deletion based on the employee relation constraint.

No timelog entry is created - this operation purely removes the timer.

Return 204 No Content on success.

Return 404 if timer does not exist or belongs to another employee.

Return 403 if the authenticated user does not have permission to discard this timer (not the owner).

parameters.description: UUID of the timer to discard (scoped to the authenticated employee's active timer)
parameters.name: timerId

prerequisites.description: Timer must be created and running before it can be discarded - the discard operation acts on an existing active timer

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated time report showing aggregated hours logged across the organization.

This operation provides comprehensive time tracking analytics with flexible grouping and filtering capabilities. Users can group results by employee, project, or task to analyze time distribution patterns. The report includes total hours, billable hours, and non-billable hours breakdowns for each group.

Supports filtering by date range (required), specific employees, projects, tasks, and billable status. Results are paginated for efficient data retrieval and support sorting by total hours, billable hours, non-billable hours, or group name.

Requires the report:view permission. All data is scoped to the user's currently selected organization. Returns 403 Forbidden if user lacks required permission, 400 Bad Request if date range is invalid.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query timelogs table with aggregation by specified grouping dimension (employee, project, or task).

Filter by date range (required), optional employee IDs, project IDs, and billable status.
Join with hrm_platform_employees for employee names, hrm_platform_projects for project names, hrm_platform_tasks for task titles.
Calculate total hours, billable hours, and non-billable hours per group.
Apply organization context filter to ensure data isolation.
Require report:view permission.
Return paginated results with sortable columns.

Edge cases:
- Empty date range returns empty result
- Invalid date range (end before start) returns 400 error
- User without report:view permission returns 403 error
- Grouping by task includes only timelogs with task assigned

responseBody.description: Paginated list of time report summaries with aggregated hours data including total hours, billable hours, and non-billable hours per group

requestBody.description: Time report search criteria including required date range, grouping dimension (employee/project/task), optional filters for employees/projects/tasks/billable status, and pagination parameters

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of project budget reports showing budget utilization statistics.

This operation provides project budget tracking by comparing allocated budget hours against actual hours logged through timelogs. Each report entry includes the project identification, budget hours, consumed hours, and utilization percentage.

Projects without budget hours are excluded from results. Supports filtering by date range, project status, and utilization threshold. Results are scoped to the user's current organization and require report:view permission.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query hrm_platform_projects table joined with hrm_platform_timelogs for aggregation. Filter projects with non-null budget_hours only (exclude projects without budget). Calculate actual hours from sum of timelog duration_minutes / 60 for each project within the requested date range. Compute budget utilization percentage as (actual_hours / budget_hours) * 100. Apply filters: date range (from timelog.date), project status, minimum utilization threshold. Sort by utilization percentage or budget consumption. Return paginated results with project summary, budget hours, actual hours, and utilization percentage. Enforce organization_id scope from authenticated user's context. Require report:view permission.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of project budget report summaries

requestBody.description: Budget report search criteria and pagination parameters

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated week-by-week summary report of time tracking data. This operation provides aggregated statistics for each week within a specified date range.

Each weekly summary includes total hours logged, number of timelog entries, and count of employees who logged time during that week. Supports optional filtering by project to focus on specific project time allocation.

Requires report:view permission. Results are organized by week (Monday to Sunday) and sorted chronologically. Pagination allows retrieval of historical data across extended date ranges. All data is scoped to the user's current organization context.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query hrm_platform_timelogs table aggregated by week (Monday to Sunday). Filter by date range from request body. Optionally filter by project_id if projectCode provided in request. Join with hrm_platform_employees to count distinct employees per week. Calculate total duration (sum of minutes converted to hours), count of timelogs, and count of distinct employees per week. Apply organization context filter using member's current organization_id. Validate user has report:view permission before executing query. Return paginated results sorted by week start date descending. Handle edge case where date range spans multiple years. Ensure weeks are properly aligned to Monday-Sunday boundaries based on organization timezone.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of weekly summary statistics

requestBody.description: Search criteria including date range, optional project filter, and pagination parameters

operations.description:
Retrieve personalized dashboard data for the current user's organization context.

This endpoint provides a comprehensive overview of time tracking activity and pending actions tailored to the user's role and permissions. For employees, the dashboard displays personal time tracking metrics including hours logged today and the current week, active timer status if running, the five most recent timelog entries, current week's timesheet submission status, and tasks assigned to the user that are open or in progress.

For users with report:view permission, the dashboard additionally includes organization-wide analytics such as count of active employees, aggregate hours logged across the organization this week, number of timesheets pending approval, projects with budget utilization tracking, and top performers ranked by hours logged. All data is scoped to the user's currently selected organization context.

The response structure adapts dynamically based on the authenticated user's role and permissions within the organization.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query dashboard data based on user's role and permissions.

For employees: Query hrm_platform_timelogs for today's and this week's total duration_minutes. Query hrm_platform_timers for active timer status (employee_id = current user). Query hrm_platform_timesheets for current week's draft/submitted status. Query hrm_platform_tasks for tasks assigned to employee with status 'open' or 'in-progress'. Query hrm_platform_timelogs for last 5 recent entries ordered by date DESC.

For users with report:view permission: Query hrm_platform_employees count where status='active'. Query hrm_platform_timelogs sum for organization-wide weekly hours. Query hrm_platform_timesheets count where status='submitted'. Query hrm_platform_projects with budget_hours and calculate utilization from timelogs. Query top 5 employees by weekly timelog duration.

Apply organization_id filter from user's current context on all queries. Return computed dashboard object with all requested sections.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of activity log entries for the organization.

This endpoint provides access to the organization's audit trail, allowing users with appropriate permissions to search and browse significant actions that have occurred. Activity logs capture employee lifecycle events, contract changes, project actions, task status changes, timesheet workflow events, and role assignments.

Supports filtering by action type, user who performed the action, and date ranges. Results are paginated with configurable page sizes and sorting options. Only users with org:manage permission can access this endpoint.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_platform_activity_logs table with pagination and filtering capabilities.

Apply filters based on request criteria:
- actionType: exact match on action_type column
- userId: filter by user_id (the actor who performed the action)
- dateFrom: created_at >= dateFrom
- dateTo: created_at <= dateTo
- targetEntityType: filter by target_entity_type column

Join with hrm_platform_users to include actor information in summary response.
Enforce organization context - only return logs for the current organization.
Verify user has org:manage permission before allowing access.

Support cursor-based or offset pagination. Default sort by created_at DESC (newest first).
Return IHrmPlatformActivityLog.ISummary for each entry with essential fields:
id, timestamp, actionType, targetEntity, actor summary, and brief details.

Handle edge cases:
- Empty result set: return empty array with pagination metadata
- Invalid date range: return 400 Bad Request
- Unauthorized access: return 403 Forbidden

responseBody.description: Paginated list of activity log summaries

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering activity logs

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific activity log entry by its unique identifier.

This operation returns the complete details of a single activity log record from the hrm_platform_activity_logs table, including the timestamp when the action occurred (created_at), the member who performed the action (member_id), the action type classification, the target entity type and ID affected by the action, and any additional metadata stored in the details JSON field. Activity logs are immutable audit records automatically created by the system for significant organizational events such as employee lifecycle changes, contract modifications, project actions, task status changes, timesheet workflow events, and role assignments.

Only members with organization management (org:manage) permission can access activity log entries. The operation enforces organization data isolation by verifying the activity log's organization_id matches the authenticated user's current organization context. Records with deleted_at timestamps are excluded from results.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query hrm_platform_activity_logs table by primary key id. Verify the activity log belongs to the user's current organization by checking organization_id matches the authenticated user's organization context. Ensure user has org:manage permission before returning the record. Return the full activity log entry including all fields: id, organization_id, member_id, action_type, target_entity_type, target_entity_id, details, created_at, updated_at. Join with hrm_platform_members table to include actor information if needed for response enrichment. Handle 404 if activity log not found or doesn't belong to user's organization. Activity logs are immutable audit records with no soft delete filtering needed for viewing.

responseBody.description: Complete activity log entry with all audit trail details including id, organization_id, member_id, action_type, target_entity_type, target_entity_id, details, created_at, and updated_at

parameters.name: activityLogId

operations.description:
Retrieve the currently selected organization context for the authenticated member.

This endpoint returns the complete organization details that the user is currently working within. All subsequent API operations are scoped to this organization context, ensuring strict data isolation in the multi-tenant platform.

The response includes organization configuration such as name, description, logo image, currency code, timezone, and fiscal year start month. This information is essential for the UI to display organization-specific branding and configure date/time displays according to the organization's settings.

Members belonging to multiple organizations must switch organization context to change which organization this endpoint returns. The organization context is maintained throughout the session until explicitly changed or the session ends.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Retrieve the currently selected organization for the authenticated member from session context.

Query hrm_platform_organizations table using the organization_id stored in the member's active session.

Return full organization entity including: id, name, description, logo, currency, timezone, fiscal_start_month, created_at, updated_at.

Enforce that the member belongs to this organization by verifying the hrm_platform_employees record exists with matching user_id and organization_id.

Return 403 if no organization context is selected or member doesn't belong to the organization.

Return 404 if organization not found or is soft-deleted (deleted_at is not null).

responseBody.description: Full organization details for the current context

operations.description:
Select the user's active organization context to work within a specific organization.

This operation allows authenticated members who belong to multiple organizations to change their working context without logging out. The system validates membership by querying the hrm_platform_employees table to confirm the user has an employee record linking them to the specified organization.

After successful selection, all subsequent API requests are scoped to the newly selected organization. The user's session remains active in hrm_platform_member_sessions, and only the organization context changes. The response includes complete organization details from hrm_platform_organizations including name, description, logo, currency, timezone, and fiscal year configuration.

This is a session-level operation that does not generate activity log entries in hrm_platform_activity_logs, as organization context selection is handled as local session management rather than a business action.
operations.name: select
operations.specification: Validate the organizationId parameter is a valid UUID format. Query hrm_platform_employees table to verify the authenticated user has an employee record in the specified organization. If no employee record exists, reject with 403 Forbidden. Update the user's session context to set the new organization ID as the active context. Return the organization details from hrm_platform_organizations table including id, name, description, logo, currency, timezone, and fiscal_start_month. Do not log this action in activity_logs as it is session management. Ensure all subsequent requests use the new organization context for data isolation.

responseBody.description: Organization details confirming the successful context selection

parameters.description: UUID of the organization to select (user must be a member)
parameters.name: organizationId

operations.description:
Stop the employee's running timer and create a timelog entry.

This operation stops the currently active timer for the authenticated employee and automatically generates a timelog record. The duration is calculated from the timer's start timestamp to the stop time, rounded to the nearest minute.

The created timelog inherits the project, task, and description from the stopped timer. The timelog date is set to the date when the timer was stopped. After successful stop, the timer is soft-deleted (marked with deleted_at timestamp) and the employee can start a new timer if needed.

Employees can only stop their own timer. If no active timer exists, the request is rejected with 404 error. The operation returns the created timelog for immediate verification of the tracked time.
operations.name: stop
operations.specification:
1. Retrieve the authenticated employee's active timer from hrm_platform_timers table.
2. If no timer exists, return 404 error (employee has no running timer).
3. Calculate duration: stop_timestamp - started_at (in milliseconds).
4. Convert duration to minutes and round to nearest minute (Math.round(durationMs / 60000)).
5. If duration is less than 30 seconds (< 0.5 minutes), set duration to 1 minute.
6. Create timelog in hrm_platform_timelogs with:
   - employee_id: from timer
   - project_id: from timer
   - task_id: from timer (nullable)
   - date: stop_timestamp date component (YYYY-MM-DD)
   - duration_minutes: calculated rounded duration
   - description: from timer (nullable)
   - billable: true (default)
7. Delete the timer record from hrm_platform_timers.
8. Return the created timelog.
9. Emit timer stop event with duration, project, task, description, billable flag.
10. Emit timelog created event.

responseBody.description: The created timelog entry with calculated duration

operations.description:
Permanently discard the employee's currently running timer without creating a timelog entry.

This operation permanently removes the active timer session for the authenticated employee. Unlike stopping a timer, discarding does not create any timelog record - the tracked time is abandoned with no entry in the system. This is useful for canceling accidental timer starts or test sessions.

The operation emits a timer discard notification event to inform real-time dashboards and subscribers that the timer session has been abandoned. After discarding, the employee can start a new timer immediately.

This operation performs a hard delete on the timer record. The discarded timer data is returned in the response for client confirmation, but no permanent record of the tracked time is retained in the system.
operations.name: discard
operations.specification:
Implementation guidance for POST /timers/discard:

1. Validate the authenticated employee has an active timer running
   - Query hrm_platform_timers table where employee_id matches authenticated user
   - If no active timer found, reject with 404 Not Found or 400 Bad Request

2. Verify timer ownership
   - Ensure the timer belongs to the authenticated employee
   - Reject if employee does not own the timer (should not happen with proper auth context)

3. Delete the timer record
   - Permanently remove the timer from hrm_platform_timers table
   - Do NOT create any timelog entry (this is the key difference from stop operation)
   - Do NOT record any activity log for discard (per requirements, discard leaves no record)

4. Emit timer discard event
   - Publish timer discard notification to real-time event system
   - Event payload includes timer ID, project, optional task, and discard timestamp
   - This allows live dashboards to update timer status in real-time

5. Return discarded timer details
   - Response includes the timer data that was discarded
   - Allows client to confirm what was abandoned
   - Include project, task, description, start time, and elapsed duration

6. Error handling
   - No active timer: 404 Not Found or 400 Bad Request with clear message
   - Authentication failure: 401 Unauthorized
   - Database error: 500 Internal Server Error

responseBody.description: Snapshot of the discarded timer session before permanent removal

operations.description:
Submit a draft timesheet for approval review.

This operation transitions a timesheet from draft status to submitted status, initiating the approval workflow. The employee who owns the timesheet can submit it when they have completed logging all time entries for the week.

The system validates that the timesheet contains at least one timelog entry and that no other timesheet for the same week has already been submitted or approved. Upon successful submission, all timelogs included in the timesheet are locked from editing or deletion through business logic validation - the timelogs remain in the database with their soft-delete capability intact, but modification operations will be rejected while the timesheet is in submitted or approved status.

Users with time:approve permission will see the submitted timesheet in their approval queue for review. The timesheet status changes to 'submitted' and cannot be modified by the employee until it is either approved or rejected. The submitted_at timestamp is recorded to track when the timesheet entered the approval workflow.
operations.name: submit
operations.specification: Submit a draft timesheet for approval workflow. Query hrm_platform_timesheets by timesheetId. Validate timesheet exists and belongs to the requesting employee. Validate timesheet status is 'draft' - reject if already submitted, approved, or rejected. Validate timesheet has at least one associated timelog in hrm_platform_timelogs - reject empty timesheets. Validate no other timesheet exists for the same employee and week_start_date with status 'submitted' or 'approved' using the unique constraint @@unique([employee_id, week_start_date]). Update timesheet: set status to 'submitted', set submitted_at to current timestamp. Lock all included timelogs from further editing or deletion. Return the updated timesheet entity. Error cases: 404 if timesheet not found, 400 if not in draft status, 400 if no timelogs, 409 if duplicate week submission exists, 403 if not the timesheet owner.

responseBody.description: Updated timesheet entity with submitted status

prerequisites.description: A draft timesheet must be created before it can be submitted for approval
At least one timelog entry must exist in the timesheet - submission is rejected for empty timesheets

operations.description:
Approve a submitted timesheet, transitioning it to approved status and enforcing immutability on all included timelogs.

This operation is restricted to users with time:approve permission within the organization. When a timesheet is approved, all timelogs included in the timesheet become immutable - they cannot be edited or deleted through the API. The system records the approval timestamp and the employee who performed the approval.

The timesheet must be in submitted status to be approved. Attempting to approve a draft, already approved, or rejected timesheet will result in an error. After approval, the timesheet status becomes approved and cannot return to draft or submitted status. Timelog immutability is enforced through business logic validation that checks the parent timesheet status before allowing modifications.
operations.name: approve
operations.specification: Validate the requesting user has time:approve permission within the current organization context. Query hrm_platform_timesheets table by timesheetId. Verify the timesheet status is 'submitted' - reject if draft, approved, or rejected. Verify the requesting employee has time:approve permission through their role assignments. Update the timesheet: set status to 'approved', set reviewed_at to current timestamp, set reviewed_by_employee_id to the requesting employee's ID. Lock all timelogs associated with this timesheet by updating their locked status. Create an activity log entry recording the approval action. Return the updated timesheet entity with all fields including the new review metadata. Handle edge cases: timesheet not found (404), insufficient permissions (403), invalid status for approval (400).

responseBody.description: The approved timesheet entity with review metadata

prerequisites.description: Timesheet must be created in draft status before it can be submitted and approved
Timesheet must be submitted (transitioned from draft to submitted status) before it can be approved

operations.description:
Reject a submitted timesheet and return it to draft status for employee revision.

This operation allows users with time:approve permission to reject a submitted timesheet. The rejection requires a reason explaining why the timesheet was rejected. Upon rejection, the timesheet status changes from 'submitted' back to 'draft', allowing the employee to modify the timelogs and resubmit.

The system records the rejection timestamp, the rejecting user, and the rejection reason. The employee receives notification of the rejection and can view the reason when accessing their timesheet.

Only timesheets in 'submitted' status can be rejected. Attempting to reject a draft, approved, or already-rejected timesheet will fail with a validation error.
operations.name: reject
operations.specification:
Reject a submitted timesheet and return it to draft status.

Implementation steps:
1. Validate timesheet exists and is not soft-deleted
2. Verify timesheet status is 'submitted' (cannot reject draft, approved, or already rejected)
3. Verify requesting user has 'time:approve' permission in the organization
4. Validate rejection_reason is provided and non-empty (required field)
5. Update timesheet: set status to 'draft', reviewed_at to current timestamp, rejection_reason to provided value, reviewed_by_employee_id to current employee's ID
6. Log activity: record timesheet rejection event in hrm_platform_activity_logs
7. Return updated timesheet entity

Edge cases:
- Rejecting a non-submitted timesheet → 400 Bad Request
- Missing rejection_reason → 400 Bad Request
- User without time:approve permission → 403 Forbidden
- Timesheet not found → 404 Not Found

responseBody.description: Updated timesheet entity with draft status and rejection metadata

requestBody.description: Rejection details including required reason

prerequisites.description: Timesheet must be created in draft status before it can be submitted and subsequently rejected
Timesheet must be submitted (status='submitted') before it can be rejected; only submitted timesheets are eligible for rejection

Backend receives this plaintext token string and validates it against hrm_platform_guest_sessions table by: (1) querying for active session where expired_at > current time, (2) validating token matches (via hash comparison or JWT verification depending on implementation). On successful validation: generates new access/refresh token pair, extends session expired_at. On failure: returns 401 Unauthorized. The token value itself is not stored as-is in the database.

IHrmPlatformGuest.IRefresh.description: Request body for renewing a guest session. Contains the refresh token issued during guest join or previous refresh operation. The token is validated against the guest sessions table to generate new authentication tokens for continued anonymous access.
IHrmPlatformGuest.IRefresh.x-autobe-specification: Request DTO for guest session refresh. Contains single refreshToken string property which is NOT a direct DB column mapping. Backend validates the provided token by querying hrm_platform_guest_sessions: checks session exists, verifies expired_at > current time, and validates token (implementation-specific, may use token hash comparison or JWT validation). On success: generates new JWT access/refresh token pair, updates session's expired_at and refreshable_until timestamps. On failure (invalid, expired, or not found): returns 401 Unauthorized. This DTO is used by POST /hrmPlatform/auth/guest/refresh endpoint.

IHrmPlatformTimer.description: Active timer session for real-time time tracking. Records the start timestamp, associated project, optional task, and work description. Each employee can have at most one active timer at a time. When stopped, timers convert to timelog entries with calculated duration.
IHrmPlatformTimer.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_timers table. Columns: id, started_at, description, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. Relations: employee via JOIN to hrm_platform_employees (ISummary), project via JOIN to hrm_platform_projects (ISummary), task via LEFT JOIN to hrm_platform_tasks (ISummary, nullable). id.description: Unique identifier for the activity log entry.

action_type.description: Classification of the action performed (e.g., employee.invited, task.status_changed, timesheet.approved).
action_type.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_activity_logs.action_type. Examples: employee.invited, employee.deactivated, contract.created, project.archived, task.status_changed, timesheet.submitted, role.assigned.

target_entity_type.description: Type of entity affected by the action (e.g., employee, project, task, timesheet).
target_entity_type.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_activity_logs.target_entity_type. Examples: employee, contract, project, task, timesheet, role.

target_entity_id.description: UUID of the affected entity, or null if the action has no specific entity target.
target_entity_id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_activity_logs.target_entity_id. Nullable for actions without specific entity target.

details.description: Structured metadata about the action in JSON format, containing action-specific details like old/new values or context.
details.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_activity_logs.details. JSON string containing action-specific metadata like old/new values, reasons, or context. Nullable.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the activity log was created (when the action occurred).
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_activity_logs.created_at. ISO 8601 date-time format.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the activity log was last updated. Static for immutable audit records.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_activity_logs.updated_at. ISO 8601 date-time format. Static for append-only audit logs.

IHrmPlatformActivityLog.description: Complete activity log entry representing an immutable audit trail record of significant organizational actions including employee lifecycle events, contract changes, project actions, task status changes, timesheet workflow, and role assignments.
IHrmPlatformActivityLog.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_activity_logs with organization and member relations joined. organization_id and member_id FK columns are transformed to $ref objects (IHrmPlatformOrganization.ISummary and IHrmPlatformMember.ISummary). deleted_at excluded as soft delete indicator not exposed in Read DTO.

IHrmPlatformTimesheet.description: Complete timesheet entity representing a weekly collection of timelogs with approval workflow. Includes week period (Monday to Sunday), workflow status (draft, submitted, approved, rejected), submission and review timestamps, rejection reason when applicable, owning employee details, reviewer employee details when reviewed, and all associated timelog entries. Used for viewing individual timesheet details and as the response for create, update, submit, approve, and reject operations.
IHrmPlatformTimesheet.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_timesheets: id (UUID), employee_id (UUID FK), reviewed_by_employee_id (UUID FK, nullable), week_start_date (ISO date YYYY-MM-DD), week_end_date (ISO date YYYY-MM-DD), status (enum: draft|submitted|approved|rejected), submitted_at (timestamp, nullable), reviewed_at (timestamp, nullable), rejection_reason (string, nullable), created_at (timestamp), updated_at (timestamp), deleted_at (timestamp, nullable). Relations: employee via JOIN to hrm_platform_employees (BELONGS-TO, use IHrmPlatformEmployee.ISummary), reviewedByEmployee via LEFT JOIN to hrm_platform_employees (BELONGS-TO, nullable, use IHrmPlatformEmployee.ISummary), timelogs via JOIN to hrm_platform_timelogs where timesheet_id matches (HAS-MANY composition, array of IHrmPlatformTimelog). Business rules: week_start_date must be Monday, week_end_date must be Sunday (week_start_date + 6 days). Unique constraint on employee_id + week_start_date. Status transitions: draft → submitted → approved|rejected (rejected → draft for resubmission). Approved timesheets lock all timelogs from editing/deletion.

histories_count.description: Number of status change history entries for this task.
histories_count.x-autobe-specification: Computed COUNT of related hrm_platform_task_histories records where hrm_platform_task_id equals this task's id. Aggregate via COUNT(*) JOIN or separate query. Returns integer >= 0.

timelogs_count.description: Number of time entries logged against this task.
timelogs_count.x-autobe-specification: Computed COUNT of related hrm_platform_timelogs records where task_id equals this task's id. Aggregate via COUNT(*) JOIN or separate query. Returns integer >= 0.

timers_count.description: Number of active timers running against this task.
timers_count.x-autobe-specification: Computed COUNT of related hrm_platform_timers records where task_id equals this task's id. Aggregate via COUNT(*) JOIN or separate query. Returns integer >= 0 (typically 0 or 1 for active timer).

IHrmPlatformTask.description: Complete task entity within a project, including all attributes, relations to project and assignee, parent task reference for subtasks, and aggregated child entities (subtasks, task histories, timelogs, and timers).
IHrmPlatformTask.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_tasks: id, title, description, status, priority, estimated_hours, due_date, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. Relations: project via JOIN to hrm_platform_projects (BELONGS-TO), assignee via JOIN to hrm_platform_employees (BELONGS-TO, nullable), parentTask via self-JOIN (BELONGS-TO, nullable). Aggregations: subtasks (recursive HAS-MANY), histories (HAS-MANY to hrm_platform_task_histories), timelogs (HAS-MANY to hrm_platform_timelogs), timers (HAS-MANY to hrm_platform_timers). All timestamps in ISO 8601 format.

actionType.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to action_type column. Exact match filter on action classification (e.g., employee.invited, contract.created).

userId.description: Filter by the member who performed the action
userId.x-autobe-specification: Maps to member_id column. UUID exact match filter for the member who performed the action.

dateTo.description: Filter logs created on or before this timestamp
dateTo.x-autobe-specification: Computed filter on created_at column. Applies created_at <= dateTo. ISO 8601 date-time format.

targetEntityType.description: Filter by affected entity type (e.g., employee, contract, project, task)
targetEntityType.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to target_entity_type column. Exact match filter on affected entity type (e.g., employee, contract, project, task).

page.description: Page number for pagination (1-based, defaults to 1)
page.x-autobe-specification: Computed pagination parameter. 1-based page number, defaults to 1. Not a DB column - used for OFFSET calculation: OFFSET = (page - 1) * limit.

limit.description: Number of items per page (defaults to 20, max 100)
limit.x-autobe-specification: Computed pagination parameter. Items per page, range 1-100, defaults to 20. Not a DB column - used for LIMIT clause.

IHrmPlatformActivityLog.IRequest.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering activity logs. Supports filtering by action type, user who performed the action, date ranges, and target entity type. All parameters are optional.
IHrmPlatformActivityLog.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: Query parameters for filtering and paginating hrm_platform_activity_logs. Maps: actionType → action_type (exact match), userId → member_id (UUID exact match), targetEntityType → target_entity_type (exact match), dateFrom → created_at >= value, dateTo → created_at <= value. Pagination: page (1-based, default 1), limit (1-100, default 20). All fields optional. Backend enforces organization_id from JWT context - never user-provided. Results sorted by created_at DESC.

startDate.description: Start date of the reporting period (inclusive). ISO 8601 date format (YYYY-MM-DD). Defines the beginning of the date range for weekly aggregation.
startDate.x-autobe-specification: ISO date string (YYYY-MM-DD) defining the inclusive start boundary of the reporting period. Backend filters hrm_platform_timelogs WHERE work_date >= startDate. Used to determine the first week to include in aggregation.

endDate.description: End date of the reporting period (inclusive). ISO 8601 date format (YYYY-MM-DD). Defines the end of the date range for weekly aggregation.
endDate.x-autobe-specification: ISO date string (YYYY-MM-DD) defining the inclusive end boundary of the reporting period. Backend filters hrm_platform_timelogs WHERE work_date <= endDate. Used to determine the last week to include in aggregation.

projectCode.description: Optional project code filter. When provided, limits results to timelogs associated with the specified project. Uses project code (not UUID) for human-readable filtering.
projectCode.x-autobe-specification: Optional project code string for filtering results to a specific project. Backend looks up project_id from hrm_platform_projects WHERE code = projectCode, then filters timelogs WHERE project_id = matched_id. If omitted, includes all projects in the organization.

page.description: Page number for pagination (1-indexed). Minimum value is 1. Determines which page of weekly summary results to retrieve.
page.x-autobe-specification: 1-indexed page number for pagination. Backend calculates OFFSET = (page - 1) * limit. Minimum value is 1. Defaults to 1 if not provided. Controls which page of weekly results to return.

limit.description: Maximum number of weekly summaries per page. Must be between 1 and 100. Controls the page size for paginated results.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Number of records per page. Backend uses as LIMIT clause. Constrained between 1 and 100. Controls the maximum number of weekly summaries returned in one response.

IHrmPlatformWeeklySummaryReport.IRequest.description: Request parameters for querying weekly time tracking summary reports. Specifies the date range for aggregation, optional project filter, and pagination controls for retrieving paginated weekly statistics.
IHrmPlatformWeeklySummaryReport.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: Query parameters for weekly summary report endpoint. Filters hrm_platform_timelogs by: (1) date range using startDate/endDate inclusive boundaries, (2) optional project_id via projectCode lookup in hrm_platform_projects. Aggregates timelogs by week (Monday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59 in organization timezone). Computes: totalHours = SUM(duration_minutes)/60, timelogCount = COUNT(*), employeeCount = COUNT(DISTINCT employee_id). Joins hrm_platform_employees for employee context, filters by member's current organization_id. Pagination via page/limit applies to weekly result set. Results sorted by weekStart descending. Requires report:view permission.

personal.description: Personal time tracking metrics including hours logged today and this week, active timer status, recent timelog entries, current timesheet status, and tasks assigned to the user.
personal.x-autobe-specification: Aggregates personal time tracking data: (1) SUM duration_minutes from hrm_platform_timelogs WHERE employee_id = current AND date = CURRENT_DATE for hoursToday. (2) SUM duration_minutes WHERE employee_id = current AND date BETWEEN week_start AND week_end for hoursThisWeek. (3) SELECT * FROM hrm_platform_timers WHERE employee_id = current AND deleted_at IS NULL for activeTimer. (4) SELECT * FROM hrm_platform_timelogs WHERE employee_id = current ORDER BY date DESC LIMIT 5 for recentTimelogs. (5) SELECT status FROM hrm_platform_timesheets WHERE employee_id = current AND week_start = current_week_start for timesheetStatus. (6) SELECT * FROM hrm_platform_tasks WHERE assignee_id = current AND status IN ('open', 'in-progress') for assignedTasks. All queries use current employee_id from JWT session.

organization.description: Organization-wide analytics including active employee count, total hours logged this week, pending timesheets awaiting approval, projects with high budget utilization, and top performers by hours logged. Null if user lacks report:view permission.
organization.x-autobe-specification: Aggregates organization-wide analytics (only if user has report:view permission, otherwise returns null): (1) COUNT FROM hrm_platform_employees WHERE organization_id = current AND status = 'active' for activeEmployeeCount. (2) SUM duration_minutes FROM hrm_platform_timelogs WHERE organization_id = current AND date BETWEEN week_start AND week_end for totalWeeklyHours. (3) COUNT FROM hrm_platform_timesheets WHERE organization_id = current AND status = 'submitted' for pendingTimesheetsCount. (4) SELECT projects WHERE budget_hours IS NOT NULL AND (SUM(timelogs.duration_minutes) / budget_hours * 100) > 80 for highBudgetUtilizationProjects. (5) SELECT employee_id, SUM(duration_minutes) FROM hrm_platform_timelogs WHERE organization_id = current GROUP BY employee_id ORDER BY SUM DESC LIMIT 5 for topPerformers. All queries filtered by organization_id from user's current context.

IHrmPlatformDashboard.description: Dashboard response containing personalized time tracking metrics and activity overview. For employees: displays hours logged today and this week, active timer status if running, five most recent timelog entries, current week's timesheet submission status, and tasks assigned to the user. For users with report:view permission: additionally includes organization-wide analytics such as active employee count, total weekly hours logged, pending timesheet count, projects with high budget utilization, and top performers by hours logged.
IHrmPlatformDashboard.x-autobe-specification: Computed dashboard type aggregating multiple sources. Personal section: Query hrm_platform_timelogs for today's (date = CURRENT_DATE) and weekly (week_start to week_end) duration_minutes sum. Query hrm_platform_timers where employee_id = current AND deleted_at = null for activeTimer. Query hrm_platform_timelogs ORDER BY date DESC LIMIT 5 for recentTimelogs. Query hrm_platform_timesheets for current week status (draft/submitted/none). Query hrm_platform_tasks where assignee_id = current AND status IN ('open', 'in-progress') for assignedTasks. Organization section (report:view permission only): Count hrm_platform_employees WHERE status = 'active'. Sum hrm_platform_timelogs duration_minutes for organization this week. Count hrm_platform_timesheets WHERE status = 'submitted'. Query hrm_platform_projects WITH budget_hours, calculate (logged_hours / budget_hours * 100) > 80. Top 5 employees by weekly timelog duration. All queries filtered by organization_id from user context. Returns null for organization section if user lacks report:view permission.

group_type.description: The grouping dimension for this report entry. Indicates whether hours are aggregated by employee, project, or task.
group_type.x-autobe-specification: Query parameter value echoed in response. Determines which entity reference (employee/project/task) is populated. Values: 'employee', 'project', 'task'.

employee.description: Employee reference when grouped by employee. Null when grouped by project or task.
employee.x-autobe-specification: LEFT JOIN to hrm_platform_employees via timelogs.employee_id. Returns IHrmPlatformEmployee.ISummary when group_type='employee', otherwise null.

project.description: Project reference when grouped by project. Null when grouped by employee or task.
project.x-autobe-specification: LEFT JOIN to hrm_platform_projects via timelogs.project_id. Returns IHrmPlatformProject.ISummary when group_type='project', otherwise null.

task.description: Task reference when grouped by task. Null when grouped by employee or project.
task.x-autobe-specification: LEFT JOIN to hrm_platform_tasks via timelogs.task_id. Returns IHrmPlatformTask.ISummary when group_type='task', otherwise null.

total_hours.description: Total hours worked in this grouping dimension. Sum of billable and non-billable hours.
total_hours.x-autobe-specification: SUM(timelogs.duration_minutes) / 60.0. Rounded to 2 decimal places. Includes all timelogs in the group regardless of billable status.

billable_hours.description: Hours worked on billable tasks. Timelogs marked as billable only.
billable_hours.x-autobe-specification: SUM(timelogs.duration_minutes WHERE timelogs.billable = true) / 60.0. Rounded to 2 decimal places.

non_billable_hours.description: Hours worked on non-billable tasks. Timelogs marked as non-billable only.
non_billable_hours.x-autobe-specification: SUM(timelogs.duration_minutes WHERE timelogs.billable = false) / 60.0. Rounded to 2 decimal places.

IHrmPlatformTimeReport.ISummary.description: Time report summary showing aggregated hours for a single grouping dimension (employee, project, or task). Includes total hours worked with billable and non-billable breakdown. Used in paginated time report responses.
IHrmPlatformTimeReport.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation from hrm_platform_timelogs. JOIN to hrm_platform_employees, hrm_platform_projects, hrm_platform_tasks based on group_type. Calculations: total_hours = SUM(duration_minutes) / 60, billable_hours = SUM(duration_minutes WHERE billable=true) / 60, non_billable_hours = SUM(duration_minutes WHERE billable=false) / 60. group_type determines which entity reference (employee/project/task) is populated; others are null. Organization context applied via employee.organization_id filter.

weekStart.description: Start date of the week period (Monday at 00:00:00).
weekStart.x-autobe-specification: Computed: First day of the ISO week period (Monday 00:00:00). Derived by grouping timelog entries by ISO week and extracting the week start boundary. Format: ISO 8601 date-time.

weekEnd.description: End date of the week period (Sunday at 23:59:59).
weekEnd.x-autobe-specification: Computed: Last day of the ISO week period (Sunday 23:59:59). Derived by grouping timelog entries by ISO week and extracting the week end boundary. Format: ISO 8601 date-time.

totalHours.description: Total hours logged by all employees during the week period.
totalHours.x-autobe-specification: Computed: SUM(duration_minutes) / 60 from hrm_platform_timelogs for all entries within the week period. Result is a decimal number representing total hours logged.

timelogCount.description: Number of individual time entry records logged during the week period.
timelogCount.x-autobe-specification: Computed: COUNT(*) of hrm_platform_timelogs entries within the week period. Integer value representing the number of individual time entries.

employeeCount.description: Number of unique employees who logged time during the week period.
employeeCount.x-autobe-specification: Computed: COUNT(DISTINCT employee_id) from hrm_platform_timelogs JOIN hrm_platform_employees for entries within the week period. Integer value representing unique employees who logged time.

IHrmPlatformWeeklySummaryReport.ISummary.description: Weekly summary statistics for time tracking reports. Contains aggregated hours logged, timelog entry count, and unique employee count for a specific week period (Monday to Sunday). Used in organization-level time reports to show weekly activity trends.
IHrmPlatformWeeklySummaryReport.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation type derived from hrm_platform_timelogs JOIN hrm_platform_employees ON employee_id. Grouping: ISO week boundaries (Monday 00:00:00 to Sunday 23:59:59). Aggregations: totalHours = SUM(duration_minutes) / 60, timelogCount = COUNT(*), employeeCount = COUNT(DISTINCT employee_id). Filters: organization_id from authenticated member context, optional project_id from request, optional date range from request. Sort order: weekStart descending (most recent weeks first). Edge cases handled: weeks spanning year boundaries use ISO week calculation, weeks with zero timelogs are excluded from results.

id.description: Unique identifier for the member account.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_members.id (UUID primary key).

avatar_image.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_members.avatar_image (nullable string, max 80000 chars). URL to user's avatar/profile image.

phone_number.description: Member's phone number for contact. Null if not provided.
phone_number.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_members.phone_number (nullable string). User's phone number for contact.

IHrmPlatformMember.ISummary.description: Lightweight member profile summary for display in lists and references. Contains essential identification fields: unique identifier, display name, optional avatar image URL, and optional phone number. Used across employee records, session tracking, invitations, task history, and activity logs to identify members without exposing sensitive account data.
IHrmPlatformMember.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_members table. Includes only essential display fields for lightweight member references: id (UUID), display_name (string), avatar_image (nullable string), phone_number (nullable string). Excludes sensitive fields (email, password_hash), system timestamps (created_at, updated_at, deleted_at), and all relations. Used as member reference in employee records, session tracking, invitations, task history, and activity log contexts.

hoursThisWeek.x-autobe-specification: Computed from hrm_platform_timelogs: SUM(duration_minutes) WHERE employee_id = current AND date BETWEEN week_start (Monday 00:00) AND week_end (Sunday 23:59) of current ISO week, divided by 60 to convert to decimal hours. Query uses employee_id from JWT session.

IHrmPlatformDashboard.IPersonal.description: Personal time tracking metrics and activity overview for the authenticated employee. IHrmPlatformDashboard.IPersonal.x-autobe-specification: Computed dashboard type aggregating multiple sources for the authenticated employee. hoursToday: SUM duration_minutes from hrm_platform_timelogs WHERE employee_id = current AND DATE(date) = CURRENT_DATE, converted to decimal hours (divide by 60). hoursThisWeek: SUM duration_minutes WHERE employee_id = current AND date BETWEEN week_start (Monday) AND week_end (Sunday) of current ISO week. activeTimer: SELECT from hrm_platform_timers WHERE employee_id = current AND deleted_at IS NULL, returns null if no active timer exists. recentTimelogs: SELECT from hrm_platform_timelogs WHERE employee_id = current ORDER BY date DESC LIMIT 5, returns array of ISummary objects. timesheetStatus: SELECT status from hrm_platform_timesheets WHERE employee_id = current AND week_start = current_week_start (Monday), returns 'none' if no timesheet exists for current week. assignedTasks: SELECT from hrm_platform_tasks WHERE assignee_id = current AND status IN ('open', 'in-progress'), returns array of ISummary objects.
